summary:
The Utah State Parks Adjustment Act (Public Law 118-181, enacted December 23, 2024) mandates the conveyance, without consideration, of certain federally owned lands to the State of Utah for incorporation into three designated state parks, and imposes public-use restrictions with a reversionary interest retained by the United States. The Act does not amend the U.S. Code; it operates as a freestanding statutory directive.

Section 2(a) requires the Secretary of the Interior, within 180 days of enactment, to convey by quitclaim deed, subject to valid existing rights, all right, title, and interest in Bureau of Land Management land identified for conveyance on the map entitled “Antelope Island State Park Proposal: Utah State Park Additions” (dated February 28, 2023) to the State for inclusion in Antelope Island State Park. Section 2(b) imposes a parallel 180‑day deadline and identical conveyance terms for BLM land depicted on the map “Wasatch Mountain State Park Proposal Utah State Park Additions” (dated May 3, 2024), for Wasatch Mountain State Park. In each case, the State bears all costs relating to the conveyance, including surveys and administrative costs.

Section 2(c) directs the Secretary of Agriculture, within 180 days of enactment, to convey by quitclaim deed, subject to valid existing rights and without consideration, all U.S. right, title, and interest in: (A) National Forest System land identified as an area selected for transfer on the map “S. 2136—Utah State Parks Adjustment Act” (dated September 12, 2023); and (B) any improvements on that land, for inclusion in Fremont Indian State Park. The conveyance is conditioned on: (1) the Secretary’s reservation of easements for all National Forest System roads and trails that originate at, terminate at, or traverse the conveyed land; (2) conveyance of only those water rights held by the United States (identified as 63‑44, 63‑1607, and 63‑2817 in the Utah State Engineer’s water rights database) that provide water to the Castle Rock Campground and the Belknap Historic Guard Station interpretive site; and (3) the State’s payment of reasonable survey costs if the Secretary determines a survey is necessary to establish acreage and legal description. The Secretary may enter into an agreement with the State concerning additional terms, including management of the Belknap Historic Guard Station, use and maintenance of roads and trails, continued permitted livestock grazing, Forest Service access to retained water rights, and other terms necessary for post‑conveyance management.

Section 2(d) authorizes the conveying Secretary to make minor modifications to the relevant maps, including adjustments to reflect surveys conducted under the Act. Section 2(e) requires the State to use all conveyed land for public purposes (parks, campgrounds, recreation, and permitted livestock grazing). If any conveyed parcel ceases to be so used, the parcel shall, at the discretion of the applicable Secretary, revert to the United States. The Act contains no appropriation; it solely authorizes conveyance and imposes the specified conditions.
